tools.name: api_resources_list
tools.description: Look up the Kubernetes API resource type(s) matching a specific kind you already have in mind (apiVersion, plural resource name, whether namespaced), using the server's preferred version for each match -- the same data 'kubectl api-resources' shows for that kind. Use this to discover the correct apiVersion for a kind before calling resources_get, resources_list, resources_create_or_update, resources_delete, or resources_scale, especially for CRDs whose apiVersion isn't already known.

kind.description: Required case-insensitive exact filter on kind (e.g. 'Deployment', 'Route'). Matches the same Kind across every API group and version, so the result can still contain multiple API resource entries.

tools.name: events_list
tools.description: List Kubernetes events (warnings, errors, state changes) for debugging and troubleshooting in the current cluster from all namespaces. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter events by field values (e.g. 'type=Warning', 'involvedObject.name=my-pod'). Supported fields: involvedObject.kind, involvedObject.name, involvedObject.namespace, involvedObject.uid, involvedObject.apiVersion, involvedObject.resourceVersion, involvedObject.fieldPath, reason, reportingComponent, source, type. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the events from. If not provided, will list events from all namespaces

tools.name: namespaces_list
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes namespaces in the current cluster. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter namespaces by field values (e.g. 'metadata.name=default', 'status.phase=Active'). Supported fields: metadata.name, status.phase. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

tools.name: nodes_log
tools.description: Get logs from a Kubernetes node (kubelet, kube-proxy, or other system logs). This accesses node logs through the Kubernetes API proxy to the kubelet

name.description: Name of the node to get logs from

query.description: query specifies services(s) or files from which to return logs (required). Example: "kubelet" to fetch kubelet logs, "/<log-file-name>" to fetch a specific log file from the node (e.g., "/var/log/kubelet.log" or "/var/log/kube-proxy.log")

tailLines.description: Number of lines to retrieve from the end of the logs (Optional, 0 means all logs)

tools.name: nodes_stats_summary
tools.description: Get detailed resource usage statistics from a Kubernetes node via the kubelet's Summary API. Provides comprehensive metrics including CPU, memory, filesystem, and network usage at the node, pod, and container levels. On systems with cgroup v2 and kernel 4.20+, also includes PSI (Pressure Stall Information) metrics that show resource pressure for CPU, memory, and I/O. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/understand-psi-metrics/ for details on PSI metrics

name.description: Name of the node to get stats from

tools.name: nodes_top
tools.description: List the resource consumption (CPU and memory) as recorded by the Kubernetes Metrics Server for the specified Kubernetes Nodes or all nodes in the cluster. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

label_selector.description: Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=') to filter nodes by label (Optional, only applicable when name is not provided)

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

name.description: Name of the Node to get the resource consumption from (Optional, all Nodes if not provided)

name.description: Name of the Pod to delete

tools.name: resources_create_or_update
tools.description:
Create or update a Kubernetes resource via Server-Side Apply. The manifest is the complete desired state: any field this tool previously set and the new manifest omits is removed. To edit an existing resource, fetch it with resources_get, modify it, then re-apply the full resource.
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

resource.description: Complete YAML or JSON representation of the Kubernetes resource (full desired state, not a partial patch). Include apiVersion, kind, metadata, and the full spec. For namespaced resources, include metadata.namespace to specify the target namespace; if omitted, the configured default namespace is used

tools.name: resources_delete
tools.description:
Delete a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, optionally the namespace, and its name
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

gracePeriodSeconds.description: Optional duration in seconds before the object should be deleted. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates delete immediately. If this value is nil, the default grace period for the specified type will be used

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

name.description: Name of the resource

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to delete the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will delete resource from configured namespace

tools.name: resources_get
tools.description:
Get a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, optionally the namespace, and its name
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

name.description: Name of the resource

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will get resource from configured namespace

tools.name: resources_list
tools.description:
List Kubernetes resources and objects in the current cluster by providing their apiVersion and kind and optionally the namespace and label selector. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resources (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter resources by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'metadata.name=myresource'). Supported fields vary by resource type. For Pods: metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, spec.schedulerName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown), status.podIP, status.nominatedNodeName. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

kind.description: kind of the resources (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

labelSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the resources by label

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resources from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will list resources from all namespaces

tools.name: vm_create
tools.description: Create a VirtualMachine on KubeVirt with the specified configuration, automatically resolving instance types, preferences, and container disk images. VM will be created in Halted state by default; use autostart parameter to start it immediately.

autostart.description: Optional flag to automatically start the VM after creation (sets runStrategy to Always instead of Halted). Defaults to false.

instancetype.description: Optional instance type name for the VM (e.g., 'u1.small', 'u1.medium', 'u1.large')

name.description: The name of the virtual machine

namespace.description: The namespace for the virtual machine

networks.description: Optional secondary network interfaces to attach to the VM. Each item specifies a Multus NetworkAttachmentDefinition to attach. Accepts either simple strings (NetworkAttachmentDefinition names) or objects with 'name' (interface name in VM) and 'networkName' (NetworkAttachmentDefinition name) properties. Each network creates a bridge interface on the VM.

oneOf.description: NetworkAttachmentDefinition name (used as both interface name and network name)
Network configuration with custom interface name

name.description: Interface name in the VM (optional, defaults to networkName)

performance.description: Optional performance family hint for the VM instance type (e.g., 'u1' for general-purpose, 'o1' for overcommitted, 'c1' for compute-optimized, 'm1' for memory-optimized). Defaults to 'u1' (general-purpose) if not specified.

preference.description: Optional preference name for the VM

size.description: Optional workload size hint for the VM (e.g., 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'xlarge'). Used to auto-select an appropriate instance type if not explicitly specified.

storage.description: Optional storage size for the VM's root disk when using DataSources (e.g., '30Gi', '50Gi', '100Gi'). Defaults to 30Gi. Ignored when using container disks.

workload.description: The workload for the VM. Accepts OS names (e.g., 'fedora' (default), 'ubuntu', 'centos', 'centos-stream', 'debian', 'rhel', 'opensuse', 'opensuse-tumbleweed', 'opensuse-leap') or full container disk image URLs

tools.name: vm_create_from_template
tools.description: Create a VirtualMachine from a VirtualMachineTemplate (virt-template) on KubeVirt. Processes the template server-side to substitute parameters (required values, defaults, and auto-generated values like passwords), then creates the resulting VirtualMachine in the same namespace. Cross-namespace template usage is not supported.

namespace.description: The namespace of the VirtualMachineTemplate and the resulting VirtualMachine (must be the same)

parameters.description: Parameter values to substitute in the template. Keys are parameter names (e.g. VM_NAME), values are strings. Required parameters must be provided; optional parameters use their defaults if omitted; parameters with generate/from will be auto-generated if not provided.

template_name.description: The name of the VirtualMachineTemplate to create the VM from

tools.name: vm_guest_info
tools.description: Get guest operating system information from a VirtualMachine's QEMU guest agent. Requires the guest agent to be installed and running inside the VM. Provides detailed information about the OS, filesystems, network interfaces, and logged-in users.

info_type.description: Type of information to retrieve: 'all' (default - all available info), 'os' (operating system details), 'filesystem' (disk and filesystem info), 'users' (logged-in users), 'network' (network interfaces and IPs)

name.description: The name of the virtual machine

namespace.description: The namespace of the virtual machine

tools.name: vm_lifecycle
tools.description: Manage KubeVirt VirtualMachine lifecycle: start, stop, restart, pause, or unpause a VM

action.description: The lifecycle action to perform: 'start' (changes runStrategy to Always), 'stop' (changes runStrategy to Halted), 'restart' (stops then starts the VM), 'pause' (suspends the running VMI in-place), or 'unpause' (resumes a paused VMI)

name.description: The name of the virtual machine

namespace.description: The namespace of the virtual machine

tools.name: vm_troubleshoot
tools.description: Diagnose KubeVirt VirtualMachine issues with automated root-cause detection. Collects VM status, VMI status, volumes, DataVolume/PVC state, cloud-init configuration, pod state, logs, and events, then runs heuristic checks to identify specific problems and suggest fixes. Returns a 'Detected Issues' section with CRITICAL/WARNING findings and actionable remediation steps, followed by raw diagnostic data. Use this tool FIRST whenever a user asks why a VM is not starting, stuck in Provisioning, crashlooping, failing to migrate, or exhibiting unexpected behavior. Automatically detects: missing StorageClasses, invalid PVC specs, dangerous cloud-init commands (shutdown/halt), nodeSelector migration blockers, failed migrations, and pod crashloops. If the user asks to fix or remediate the issue, use the Suggested Fixes from the report with vm_lifecycle (restart) or resources_create_or_update.

name.description: The name of the VirtualMachine to troubleshoot

namespace.description: The namespace of the VirtualMachine to troubleshoot

The `pod-reader` ServiceAccount was correctly referenced by its RoleBinding, but the bound Role had the wrong permission: it allowed `list` on `apps/deployments`, not on core `pods`.

I updated `pod-reader-role` in `simple-rbac-setup` to allow `list` on `pods`. The permission is namespace-scoped, so it applies only in `simple-rbac-setup`.

outputSteps.content:
The `pod-reader` ServiceAccount was correctly referenced by its RoleBinding, but the bound Role had the wrong permission: it allowed `list` on `apps/deployments`, not on core `pods`.

I updated `pod-reader-role` in `simple-rbac-setup` to allow `list` on `pods`. The permission is namespace-scoped, so it applies only in `simple-rbac-setup`.

Steps.message: Verification successful: RBAC role correctly reconfigured.

results.taskOutput:
Fixed the `nginx` Service selector: it was `app=web`, but the ready nginx pod is labeled `app=nginx`, so the Service had no endpoints. The Service now selects `app=nginx`, and its endpoint has populated as `10.244.0.45:8080`.

The Service is `ClusterIP` at `10.97.37.67` on port 80, so it’s reachable from within the cluster at `nginx.web.svc.cluster.local` (or `nginx` from namespace `web`). It is not exposed externally.

Steps.message:
namespace/web created
deployment.apps/nginx created
service/nginx created

Fixed the `nginx` Service selector: it was `app=web`, but the ready nginx pod is labeled `app=nginx`, so the Service had no endpoints. The Service now selects `app=nginx`, and its endpoint has populated as `10.244.0.45:8080`.

The Service is `ClusterIP` at `10.97.37.67` on port 80, so it’s reachable from within the cluster at `nginx.web.svc.cluster.local` (or `nginx` from namespace `web`). It is not exposed externally.

outputSteps.content:
Fixed the `nginx` Service selector: it was `app=web`, but the ready nginx pod is labeled `app=nginx`, so the Service had no endpoints. The Service now selects `app=nginx`, and its endpoint has populated as `10.244.0.45:8080`.

The Service is `ClusterIP` at `10.97.37.67` on port 80, so it’s reachable from within the cluster at `nginx.web.svc.cluster.local` (or `nginx` from namespace `web`). It is not exposed externally.

results.taskOutput:
The pods were stuck in `Pending` because the Deployment required a node labeled `environment=production-gpu`, but the cluster’s only Ready node didn’t have that label. With no pods scheduled, the Service had no available backends, which explains the connection errors.

I removed that node selector. The Deployment now has **2/2 ready replicas**, and `web-app-service` has endpoints on both pods at port 80. The service should now be reachable; please retry the frontend connection.

Steps.message:
namespace/webshop-frontend created
service/web-app-service created
deployment.apps/web-app-deployment created
Waiting for resources to be created...
deployment.apps/web-app-deployment condition met
Warning: v1 Endpoints is deprecated in v1.33+; use discovery.k8s.io/v1 EndpointSlice
Setup successful: Service has no endpoints as expected

The pods were stuck in `Pending` because the Deployment required a node labeled `environment=production-gpu`, but the cluster’s only Ready node didn’t have that label. With no pods scheduled, the Service had no available backends, which explains the connection errors.

I removed that node selector. The Deployment now has **2/2 ready replicas**, and `web-app-service` has endpoints on both pods at port 80. The service should now be reachable; please retry the frontend connection.

outputSteps.content:
The pods were stuck in `Pending` because the Deployment required a node labeled `environment=production-gpu`, but the cluster’s only Ready node didn’t have that label. With no pods scheduled, the Service had no available backends, which explains the connection errors.

I removed that node selector. The Deployment now has **2/2 ready replicas**, and `web-app-service` has endpoints on both pods at port 80. The service should now be reachable; please retry the frontend connection.

Created the six requested namespaces, quotas, developer service accounts, RBAC bindings, and default-deny network policies.

- **Developer namespaces:** Alice, Bob, and Charlie each have a namespace-admin RoleBinding for their named user and service account.
- **`dev-shared`:** Each developer and service account has read-only access to selected workload and configuration resources; Secrets are excluded.
- **Staging and prod:** Quotas and default-deny policies are in place. Their only configured egress exception is DNS; there are no developer access bindings in these namespaces.
- **Network isolation:** Developer namespaces allow same-namespace ingress and egress to their own namespace, `dev-shared`, and DNS. `dev-shared` permits ingress from developer namespaces and itself. Staging and prod have no ingress allowances.

**Important limitations:** The user RoleBindings use the literal usernames `alice`, `bob`, and `charlie`; confirm those match the identities your cluster’s authentication provider supplies. Kubernetes RBAC is additive, so verify that existing ClusterRoleBindings do not already grant those users access to staging or prod. DNS is allowed, but other “system services” were not specified and are not broadly permitted. NetworkPolicy enforcement also depends on the cluster’s CNI supporting NetworkPolicy.

Setting up cluster state for dev environment eval...
Setup completed successfully

Created the six requested namespaces, quotas, developer service accounts, RBAC bindings, and default-deny network policies.

- **Developer namespaces:** Alice, Bob, and Charlie each have a namespace-admin RoleBinding for their named user and service account.
- **`dev-shared`:** Each developer and service account has read-only access to selected workload and configuration resources; Secrets are excluded.
- **Staging and prod:** Quotas and default-deny policies are in place. Their only configured egress exception is DNS; there are no developer access bindings in these namespaces.
- **Network isolation:** Developer namespaces allow same-namespace ingress and egress to their own namespace, `dev-shared`, and DNS. `dev-shared` permits ingress from developer namespaces and itself. Staging and prod have no ingress allowances.

**Important limitations:** The user RoleBindings use the literal usernames `alice`, `bob`, and `charlie`; confirm those match the identities your cluster’s authentication provider supplies. Kubernetes RBAC is additive, so verify that existing ClusterRoleBindings do not already grant those users access to staging or prod. DNS is allowed, but other “system services” were not specified and are not broadly permitted. NetworkPolicy enforcement also depends on the cluster’s CNI supporting NetworkPolicy.

results.taskOutput:
- **Root cause:** `broken-vm` referenced a cloud-init Secret named `vm-cloud-init` that did not exist in `vm-test-troubleshoot`. The virt-launcher pod’s `FailedMount` event confirmed the missing Secret, preventing startup.
- **Action taken:** Created the missing Secret with basic cloud-init user data, then restarted the VM.
- **Was it successful?** Yes. The VM is now **Running** and reports **Ready=True**. The initial restart happened before the VM had cleared its retry delay, so it briefly remained in `CrashLoopBackOff`; a subsequent restart succeeded.

Steps.message: VM created with missing Secret reference - waiting for failure state

- **Root cause:** `broken-vm` referenced a cloud-init Secret named `vm-cloud-init` that did not exist in `vm-test-troubleshoot`. The virt-launcher pod’s `FailedMount` event confirmed the missing Secret, preventing startup.
- **Action taken:** Created the missing Secret with basic cloud-init user data, then restarted the VM.
- **Was it successful?** Yes. The VM is now **Running** and reports **Ready=True**. The initial restart happened before the VM had cleared its retry delay, so it briefly remained in `CrashLoopBackOff`; a subsequent restart succeeded.

outputSteps.content:
- **Root cause:** `broken-vm` referenced a cloud-init Secret named `vm-cloud-init` that did not exist in `vm-test-troubleshoot`. The virt-launcher pod’s `FailedMount` event confirmed the missing Secret, preventing startup.
- **Action taken:** Created the missing Secret with basic cloud-init user data, then restarted the VM.
- **Was it successful?** Yes. The VM is now **Running** and reports **Ready=True**. The initial restart happened before the VM had cleared its retry delay, so it briefly remained in `CrashLoopBackOff`; a subsequent restart succeeded.

results.taskOutput:
- **Root cause:** The VM’s cloud-init configuration shuts down the guest immediately after boot. Because the VM has `runStrategy: Always`, KubeVirt starts it again, creating a restart loop.
- **Command causing it:** `shutdown -h now` in cloud-init’s `runcmd`.
- **Fix:** Remove that command from the VM’s cloud-init `userData`. If shutting down after boot is intentional, change `runStrategy` to `Manual` or `Halted` instead.

Steps.message: Waiting for VM to attempt boot and crash...

- **Root cause:** The VM’s cloud-init configuration shuts down the guest immediately after boot. Because the VM has `runStrategy: Always`, KubeVirt starts it again, creating a restart loop.
- **Command causing it:** `shutdown -h now` in cloud-init’s `runcmd`.
- **Fix:** Remove that command from the VM’s cloud-init `userData`. If shutting down after boot is intentional, change `runStrategy` to `Manual` or `Halted` instead.

outputSteps.content:
- **Root cause:** The VM’s cloud-init configuration shuts down the guest immediately after boot. Because the VM has `runStrategy: Always`, KubeVirt starts it again, creating a restart loop.
- **Command causing it:** `shutdown -h now` in cloud-init’s `runcmd`.
- **Fix:** Remove that command from the VM’s cloud-init `userData`. If shutting down after boot is intentional, change `runStrategy` to `Manual` or `Halted` instead.
